THE ACADEMIC VISION
In 1930, the University of Pennsylvania
Museum, backed by Eldridge R. Johnston,
launched an ambitious expedition to extract
massive Maya monuments from the Guatemalan
jungle for public display. Directed by
J. Alden Mason and Linton Satterthwaite.

The Human Cost of History
The pristine Maya monuments sitting quietly in
the University of Pennsylvania Museum today
were not extracted by magic. They are
physical monuments to both ancient Maya
genius and 1930s human endurance.

The Legacy of the 1931 Season
The Irony.
I never want to come here again, never!
- Peggy Satterthwaite, I93I.
The Reality
Despite her protestations, Peggy returned to
Piedras Negras with Linton every single year
from 1932 to 1939.
The Legacy
The Satterthwaites transformed Maya
archaeology, excavating eleven temples, mapping
the city, and launching the career of legendary
epigrapher Tatiana Proskouriakoff. The diary
survives as a rare, unfiltered testament to the
unglamorous realities of scientific discovery.
